Rhonda Hart

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 36, Harris County, Texas · Challenger

Public policy advocate and gun-safety activist; U.S. Army veteran

Rhonda Hart is a Democrat and U.S. Army veteran (2000–2003). She became a gun-safety advocate after her 14-year-old daughter, Kimberly Vaughan, was killed in the 2018 Santa Fe High School shooting. She was the 2024 Democratic nominee in Texas' 14th Congressional District, then won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for the 36th District with 64.2% of the vote over Doug Rogers, and faces incumbent Republican Brian Babin on November 3, 2026.

Where Hart stands

Health care
Supports a woman's right to make her own health care decisions and says she would work to pass federal law codifying Roe v. Wade. Says pregnant women in Texas should not have to leave the state for life-saving care.
Health care
Lists 'Fixing Our Broken Healthcare System' among her core campaign priorities and says she has advocated for better health care access.
Gun policy
Says she has spent six years pushing for safer gun storage laws and will continue to push for gun-violence prevention laws in Congress.
Immigration / birthright citizenship
Lists 'Immigration and ICE Reform' as a core campaign priority. No detailed position on birthright citizenship was found.
Defense / veterans
Lists 'Veterans & Military' as a core priority and says she has advocated for support for military veterans, describing herself as a disabled veteran.
Voting rights
Lists 'Voting Rights & the SAVE Act' as a core campaign priority.

Background

  • U.S. Army, 2000–2003
  • Associate degree, University of Alaska Southeast, 2009
  • High school diploma, Wasilla High School (Alaska)
  • Public policy advocate; gun-safety activist since 2018
  • Democratic nominee, U.S. House Texas District 14, 2024 (lost to Randy Weber)
  • Won Democratic primary, U.S. House Texas District 36, March 3, 2026 (64.2%)
